- A new Online Co-op entry on the game's title screen. Host a co-op journey of your own and play it
  with a friend whenever you both have time; it carries on where you left off.
- Start a new co-op journey: pick the difficulty, choose the co-op settings, then begin the journey.
  Your friend can join once it first saves after the opening.
- Join Journey: type your friend's code (or use the one you copied) and you're taken into their game.
  The first time, you start with the host's Cal; after that you keep your own Cal, outfit, skills and
  finds every time you come back.
- Your journeys are listed with the planet you're on, who you play with and when you last played
  together. Delete a journey, or export it to one of your own save slots.

**Co-op settings, per journey**
- Enemy health: Normal, Tougher or Toughest. The host's choice applies to both players.
- Unlocks: Your own (each player keeps what they find) or Shared (stims, essences and chests found
  by one player count for both, and are gone from the other player's world, so nothing can be picked
  up twice). With Shared, anything found while you were away is waiting when you return.

**Recovery code**
- The launcher and the co-op menu (F4) show your recovery code. Enter it in the launcher on another
  PC to keep your progress in your friends' journeys. Keep it to yourself.

**Good to know**
- Both players need JediCoop 0.10.0 to play together. The launcher updates itself to 1.2.0 first,
  then offers JediCoop 0.10.0.
- Co-op journeys never touch your own save slots unless you export one there.

# JediCoop patch notes

## 0.10.0
**Co-op journeys**
- A new Online Co-op entry on the game's title screen. Host a co-op journey of your own and play it
  with a friend whenever you both have time; it carries on where you left off.
- Start a new co-op journey: pick the difficulty, choose the co-op settings, then begin the journey.
  Your friend can join once it first saves after the opening.
- Join Journey: type your friend's code (or use the one you copied) and you're taken into their game.
  The first time, you start with the host's Cal; after that you keep your own Cal, outfit, skills and
  finds every time you come back.
- Your journeys are listed with the planet you're on, who you play with and when you last played
  together. Delete a journey, or export it to one of your own save slots.

**Co-op settings, per journey**
- Enemy health: Normal, Tougher or Toughest. The host's choice applies to both players.
- Unlocks: Your own (each player keeps what they find) or Shared (stims, essences and chests found
  by one player count for both, and are gone from the other player's world, so nothing can be picked
  up twice). With Shared, anything found while you were away is waiting when you return.

**Recovery code**
- The launcher and the co-op menu (F4) show your recovery code. Enter it in the launcher on another
  PC to keep your progress in your friends' journeys. Keep it to yourself.

**Good to know**
- Both players need JediCoop 0.10.0 to play together. The launcher updates itself to 1.2.0 first,
  then offers JediCoop 0.10.0.
- Co-op journeys never touch your own save slots unless you export one there.

## 0.9.9
**Co-op fixes**
- The joining player no longer sees "Shortcut unlocked" for shortcuts the host had opened earlier.
- You can see the Purge troopers' shots aimed at your friend, and their shots at you hurt and can be
  parried. Rocket troopers' missiles show up too.
- Heavy gunners raise their shield in both games.
- Fixed an invisible obstacle where an enemy your friend had already defeated used to stand.
- Fixed co-op sometimes stopping for the rest of the session after the host respawned or rode a lift.
- Blocking blaster shots aimed at you now sends them back at the trooper, even when the trooper is
  being controlled from your friend's game.
- Enemies now go after whichever of you is nearer, and turn on a player their shots hit, without
  breaking off an attack halfway.
- Troopers' blasters no longer float away from their hands, and those troopers no longer jitter.
- Flametroopers' flames, baton trails and other attack effects now show in both games.
- AT-ST shots now show up for both players.
- Bounty hunters' laser sights point at the right player, and their wrist rockets explode in both
  games.
- Brute droids and bounty hunters look the same in both games.
- Defeated enemies are much less likely to go flying across the area.
- Fixed an enemy sometimes being missing in one game after a respawn.

## 0.9.8
**Co-op fixes**
- Fixed a crash when some enemies came into view, such as Purge troopers.
- Fixed a rare problem where co-op stopped working for the host while riding a lift into a new area.

## 0.9.7
**Co-op fixes**
- Shortcuts the host has opened are open for the joining player too, including ones opened in an
  earlier session.
- When your friend closes the game, you're told they left, instead of "disconnected".

## 0.9.6
**Co-op fixes**
- Force Slow on puzzle objects looks the same in both games.
- Closing the game ends the co-op session straight away, so your friend isn't left waiting.

## 0.9.5
**Choose the rules before you play**
- New Co-op settings in the launcher, next to Play: the difficulty, following your friend to another
  planet, and the size of JediCoop's messages. Choose them before you start the game; in the game
  you just host (F6) or join (F7).
- Difficulty: Normal (the game as it is), Tougher (enemies have 1.5× health) or Toughest (2×). The
  host's choice is used for both players, so you no longer have to pick the same.
- Following: Ask me (Y / N), Always follow, or Stay.
- The co-op menu (F4) shows the difficulty in use and whose choice it is.
- Both players need 0.9.5 to play together.

**Fixes**
- With Tougher or Toughest, enemies no longer get even tougher each time a player leaves and joins
  again.

## 0.9.4
**Install, Update and Play are separate buttons**
- Install (or Update) and Play are now two buttons. Install or update first and watch each step; then
  Play starts the game.
- While an update is waiting, Play says why: both players need the same version of JediCoop.
- The message under the buttons is easier to read over the background.

## 0.9.3
**See what Install and Update do**
- Install & Play and Update & Play now show each step on the button as it happens: checking the
  game, copying JediCoop's files (with their names and sizes), your settings, checking the installed
  files, and starting the game.
- If a step fails, the launcher shows which one and why, and the button offers Try again.

## 0.9.2
**A new look for the launcher**
- A new design and a new logo, with scenes from the games behind each page.
- What's new is now a page with the notes for every version. It still opens by itself after an
  update.
- Jedi: Survivor has its own page. It shows whether the game is on your PC; co-op for it comes later.
- The game folder, Uninstall and the server address are under Settings.
- Messages appear at the top of the window and never cover a button; click ✕ to dismiss one.

**Tidier install**
- The settings file now holds only the settings you might change: your name, the server, the
  difficulty and the message size. Everything else uses built-in defaults.
- The log file is shorter and easier to send when asking for help.

## 0.9.1
**Updates without reinstalling**
- The launcher now updates itself: when a new version is out, it offers "Update now", installs it in a
  few seconds and restarts. Your settings and saves stay as they are.

**Fixes**
- Joining by code over the internet could fail at once with "Can't reach the JediCoop server".
- A failed join is now shown once instead of twice.
- Save backups are named with your local time, and the launcher says which folder it made.
- Launcher messages no longer cover the buttons.

## 0.9.0
The first version with the JediCoop launcher and join codes.

**Getting started**
- The JediCoop launcher finds your game (Steam or EA app), checks it's a supported version, and
  installs, updates or removes the mod with one click. It never changes the game's own files.
- Set your name once in the launcher; press Play to start the game with JediCoop.
- Back up your saves, or import a save a friend sent you, from the launcher.

**Play together**
- Host: press F6 in the game. You get a join code (like K7Q-X9R), already copied: paste it to your
  friend. No extra software or router settings needed.
- Join: copy the code, then press F7 in the game (or press F7 and type it).
- See your friend's Cal in your game, with lightsaber, poncho and BD-1.
- Fight together: shared enemies, damage and deaths in both games; blaster bolts, acid spit and
  baton strikes from enemies the other game runs hit you too, with the game's own knockback and
  sparks. Block bolts to stop them.
- Travel separately: each player flies their own Mantis. When one picks a planet, the other is
  asked "Follow? [Y] / [N]".
- Shared world: a shortcut door unlocked by one player opens for both; Force Slow on a puzzle
  object slows it in both games.
- Difficulty: Co-op (the normal game) or Scaled (tougher enemies for two players).

**Menus and messages**
- F4 opens the co-op menu (session, join code, keys, your name, difficulty, mod version).
- Join problems are explained: a wrong code, or a different mod or game version, says so plainly.

**Safety**
- Back up your saves from the launcher before playing together (one click, dated copies).

**Known limits**
- Force Slow on an object looks different in the other player's game.
- Parrying a bolt back only works for bolts aimed at you.
- Enemies alerted far from one player may stand still in that player's game until they're defeated.
- Some enemy types and bosses are untested.
